reasons.specificity: The inventory names specific regulations (Defence Trade Controls Amendment Act 2024, Title III DPA treatment, ROK FSC decree, Japan Three Principles), specific firms (Lynas, Arafura, Hanwha, Fortescue, Red 6), and specific dollar amounts drawn from the source, giving it genuine source-specificity rather than generic AUKUS commentary, though some cells (enforcement intensity, compliance rates) are frankly marked unknown rather than fabricated.
reasons.anchoring: Most quotes are verbatim and correctly placed—'between AUKUS states without export licences,' 'more than 100 companies having left the industry,' '40 percent of its equity capital,' 'put companies who develop advanced military technology at an advantage'—and the interpretive claims they support are defensible given the passages; a few inferences (e.g. 'financier of last resort') stretch the source slightly but are not invented.
reasons.non_obviousness: The inventory surfaces several non-obvious structural points—dual-use definitional arbitrage across climate/industrial/defence funding streams, VC gaining 'power to structure' through state procurement, export-credit agency repurposing, and timing arbitrage from locking in beneficiaries before strategic performance is demonstrated—but these are largely re-expressions of the article's own analytical framework rather than independent expert distinctions the article does not itself draw.
reasons.coherence: Rule identities, actors, and effects are consistently attributed throughout the REG/EV/EF/COMP/ARB/INT sections and the findings ledger; the counter-evidence section honestly acknowledges the source's own caveats; there are no internal contradictions between the prose description and the tabular/ledger entries.
reasons.usefulness: The inventory gives a reader a structured entry point to nine distinct regulatory instruments, their interactions, arbitrage openings, and open questions, which genuinely helps navigate a dense political-economy article; however the requested 'dated reported-rule inventory' format with proposal/adoption/effect status columns is partially met rather than fully tabulated, and some entries (compliance rates, enforcement) are frankly indeterminate, limiting immediate operational utility.
reasons.hallucination_risk: No clearly invented facts, false dates, or fabricated quotes were detected; dollar figures match source passages; the Hanwha 'Redback' deal, NSSIF GBP 220 million figure, USD 886 billion defence budget, and 12% chip-production share are all traceable to source text; acknowledged unknowns are marked as such rather than filled with speculation; minor risk comes from slightly editorialised labels ('medium-low' regulatory quality) that go beyond what the source establishes.

score.one_line: A thorough, largely well-anchored regulatory inventory that faithfully maps the source's nine instruments with correct quotes and figures, though it re-expresses the article's own framework more than it adds independent expert distinctions, and its compliance/enforcement cells are necessarily indeterminate given the archive-bound source.
